artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan adding an advisory-only --gate verification tier at implement dispatch: core flag plumbing mirroring --compare, docs and metadata contract, a books-gate.sh resolve-and-run wrapper, its fixture suite, books agent/skill binding, and core test coverage.

memory_candidates.content: Advisory dispatch flags in the /orchestrate engine follow a fixed seven-site threading recipe that recurs verbatim per flag (--lit, --compare, now --gate): (1) parse-command-args.sh needs FIVE edits, not three -- doc comment, initializer, substring detector, the FOCUS_PROMPT sed strip chain, and the export list; omitting the strip chain lets the flag leak into focus-prompt text. (2) orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh carries the ONLY phase-scoping mechanism, a single guard line of the form `[ "$flag" = "true" ] && [ "$g" = "implement" ] && build_args+=(--flag)`; build_args is composed at exactly one site, so there is no second forwarding path. (3) orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh is deliberately phase-agnostic and emits the field conditionally, preserving a byte-identity invariant: a no-flag dispatch file must be byte-identical to one built before the flag existed, which its test suite asserts as 'differs by exactly one added line'. (4) Documentation lands at four layers (command Options row, the --hard composability row, skill-orchestrate Setup+Move-1, and a `### <flag> (optional)` section in return-metadata-file.md), with the advisory MUST-NOTs restated INSIDE the consuming agent step rather than in a separate section, so a later editor cannot fold an advisory branch into a status-downgrading one. The substring-regex detector shape also means no `--flag-suffix` sibling is ever safe.
